step1_analysis.description: A cross-coupled NMOS pair that provides negative resistance to compensate for losses in an LC tank, forming the active core of a voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO).

paper_reference.title: A Study of Injection Locking and Pulling in Oscillators

oscillation_frequency.description: The fundamental frequency of the free-running oscillator.

sky130_expected.calculation: f = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(L_eq * C_eq)). With L_eq = 10nH and C_eq = 3.1pF, f ≈ 900 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the LC tank components added in the testbench to match the paper's reported 900 MHz.

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the oscillator core.

sky130_expected.reasoning: A 2mA tail current is used for the SKY130 testbench to ensure reliable startup, resulting in much lower power than the 1W reported in the paper (which likely refers to a high-power discrete or PA-integrated design).

voltage_swing.description: Peak-to-peak voltage swing at the oscillator output nodes.

sky130_expected.calculation: Swing is limited by VDD and the tail current. With ideal inductors, the node can swing above VDD.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical voltage swing for a 1.8V LC oscillator with a 2mA tail current.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure the free-running oscillation frequency, power consumption, and voltage swing of the cross-coupled oscillator core.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Oscillator Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u

* DUT
XM1 N0 N2 P GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N2 N0 P GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}

* Testbench components
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
I_tail P 0 2m
L1 N0 VDD 5n
L2 N2 VDD 5n
C1 N0 N2 3.1p

* Initial condition to kickstart oscillation
.ic v(N0)=1.8 v(N2)=1.7

.control
  tran 10p 20n
  
  * Measure power consumption
  meas tran avg_current avg i(VVDD) from=10n to=20n
  let avg_power = -avg_current * 1.8
  print avg_power
  
  * Measure oscillation frequency
  meas tran t1 trig v(N0) val=1.8 rise=10
  meas tran t2 trig v(N0) val=1.8 rise=11
  let osc_freq = 1 / (t2 - t1)
  print osc_freq
  
  * Measure voltage swing
  meas tran vmax max v(N0) from=10n to=20n
  meas tran vmin min v(N0) from=10n to=20n
  let swing = vmax - vmin
  print swing
  
  quit
.endc
.end
